questions.question: D1 — Run /office-hours before the review, or proceed directly? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-office-hours>

options.label: Skip — proceed with standard review (Recommended)
options.description: Jump straight into the 4-section engineering review of the Multi-tenant Auth Refactor plan. The plan content in PLAN.md is sufficient to review. Recommended since the plan is already written.

options.label: Run /office-hours first
options.description: Run /office-hours to generate a structured design doc (problem statement, premise challenge, alternatives explored) before reviewing. Takes ~10 min but gives sharper input for the review.

questions.question: D2 — This plan introduces 4 new classes across 12 files. Recommend scope reduction before reviewing, or accept the complexity and review as-is? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-scope-challenge>

options.label: Accept complexity — review as-is (Recommended)
options.description: Proceed with the full review of all 4 classes across 12 files. Flag any specific overengineering during the Architecture section, but don't block on scope reduction now. Recommended: the scope smell is already called out in the plan and the review will surface whether it's justified.

options.label: Recommend scope reduction first
options.description: Propose a minimal version (e.g. collapse SessionMint and RequestPolicy to plain modules, reduce new classes to 2) and ask the user to confirm before reviewing the full plan. This risks re-scoping before we understand the full design rationale.

questions.question: D3 — Should gstack search learnings from your other projects on this machine when reviewing? <gstack-qid:cross-project-learnings>

options.label: Enable cross-project learnings (Recommended)
options.description: Searches learnings from all your projects on this machine for patterns that might apply here. Stays local — no data leaves your machine. Best for solo devs.

options.label: Keep learnings project-scoped only
options.description: Only searches learnings from this specific project. Best if you work on multiple client codebases where cross-contamination is a concern.

questions.question: D4 — [P1] (confidence: 9/10) Architecture — AuthBroker and SessionMint share a global mutable AuthCache. How should this be fixed? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-arch-shared-cache>

options.label: Inject AuthCache as constructor dependency (Recommended)
options.description: Pass AuthCache into AuthBroker and SessionMint at construction time. No global export. Clear ownership. Fully testable in isolation. Eliminates race window from concurrent mutations. ~30 min human / ~5 min CC. Explicit > clever, your stated preference.

options.label: Keep global export, add a mutex/lock wrapper
options.description: Wrap the global AuthCache in an async lock or mutex so concurrent mutations are serialized. Fixes the race but preserves the shared-state design, serializes all cache ops (throughput hit), and still makes tests depend on global state. ~1h human / ~10 min CC.

options.label: Accept as-is — document the concurrency risk
options.description: Add a comment noting the race condition and require callers to coordinate. Defers the real fix, leaves a known race in the auth path of a multi-tenant system. Not recommended for any production auth refactor.

questions.question: D5 — [P1] (confidence: 9/10) Code Quality — validateAndDispatch() swallows errors in 3 nested try/catch blocks. How should this be remedied? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-cq-error-swallowing>

options.label: Split into focused functions + propagate errors properly (Recommended)
options.description: Extract validate(), dispatch(), and per-error-class handlers as separate functions. Remove silent catches — each error propagates or is explicitly re-thrown with context. Result: testable, explicit, auditable. Auth errors are never silently absorbed. ~1h human / ~10 min CC. Explicit > clever.

options.label: Keep structure, add logging + re-throw on each catch
options.description: Retain the 60-line function but replace bare catch swallowing with `logger.error(err); throw new AuthError(...)`. Catches remain nested but errors are no longer silent. Easier diff, but the testability and cognitive-complexity problems remain. ~30 min human / ~5 min CC.

options.label: Accept as-is — document that each catch is intentional
options.description: Add a comment explaining why each error class is swallowed. Does not fix the silent-failure risk or the testability gap. Not recommended for auth-path code.

answers.D5 \u2014 [P1] (confidence: 9/10) Code Q: Split into focused functions + propagate errors properly (Recommended)

questions.question: D6 — [P2] (confidence: 8/10) Tests — No test planned for concurrent AuthBroker + SessionMint mutations on the shared AuthCache (even after DI fix, concurrent callers with the same injected instance can race). Add a concurrency test? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-test-concurrent>

options.label: Add a concurrency unit test (Recommended)
options.description: Write a test that fires AuthBroker.dispatch() and SessionMint.mint() simultaneously against the same AuthCache instance and asserts no phantom 401s or corrupted state. Catches races before they hit prod. ~45 min human / ~8 min CC. Completeness: 9/10.

options.label: Skip — rely on integration tests
options.description: Trust that the multi-tenant integration tests will incidentally exercise concurrent paths. Cheaper up front, but integration tests rarely simulate true concurrency and won't catch the specific race window. Completeness: 6/10.

questions.question: D7 — [P2] (confidence: 7/10) Tests — No E2E test planned for the tenant-suspended-mid-session flow (user holds a valid token when their tenant is suspended — next request should be rejected). Add it? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-test-suspend-e2e>

options.label: Add E2E test for suspend-mid-session (Recommended)
options.description: Simulate: tenant active → valid token issued → tenant suspended → subsequent request with old token → assert 401 + session cleared. This is an auth/security flow — too important to trust unit tests alone. [E2E]. ~1h human / ~10 min CC. Completeness: 9/10.

options.label: Skip — the invalidation hook test covers this
options.description: The existing adapter invalidation-hook tests (unchanged per plan) already verify that suspend triggers cache eviction. Trusts existing coverage for the full user-facing flow. Completeness: 7/10.

questions.question: D8 — [P2] (confidence: 9/10) Performance — 5 sequential IDP calls per validation, trivially parallelizable via Promise.all. Fix it in this PR or defer? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-perf-idp-parallel>

options.label: Fix it now — add Promise.all parallelization (Recommended)
options.description: Replace the 5 sequential IDP calls with Promise.all([call1, call2, call3, call4, call5]). The plan already confirms they're independent. Reduces validation latency by ~4x (e.g. 250ms → ~60ms). With CC this is a 5-minute fix. No reason to defer. ~30 min human / ~5 min CC. Completeness: 10/10.

options.label: Defer to a follow-up PR
options.description: Ship the refactor first, then optimize. Accepts the latency regression for the PR window. Only reasonable if the auth refactor is already blocked on other reviews and the 250ms is acceptable for now. Completeness: 7/10.

answers.D8 \u2014 [P2] (confidence: 9/10) Perfor: Fix it now — add Promise.all parallelization (Recommended)
